scope: Complete 56-frame 1920×1080 HDR reference at 512×288 neural processing, compared with corrected 320×192 processing. Exact input/timing, original/proxy/identity, finite output and fresh cut checks pass. This records geometry-dependent enhanced results without temporal-quality, physical HDR or source-rate playback acceptance.
geometryInterpretation: Logical pixels increase 2.4×. Exact 16:9 sampling replaces 5:3; padded model extent changes from 320×320 to 512×320 (1.6× area). Geometry affects more than scalar pixel count, so no isolated resolution-quality effect is inferred.

freshCuts.scope: Exactly two sequential fresh one-frame processes at the automatic cuts. CPU audit/review may overlap these controls; wall times are diagnostic.

wall.domain: Linear BT.2020 Y in nits. Same fixed unaligned full-resolution ROI; no mask/registration/photometric normalization.
wall.interpretation: The complete fixed, unaligned region retains enhancement variation. Metrics describe this region and apply no registration, perceptual threshold or general quality ranking.

limitations: Single offline captures with synchronous four-view readback/write; no causal speed, memory improvement, source-rate playback, quality or physical-display acceptance claim.
The logical and vendor-aligned padded model extents both differ. Equal input pixels, model and binary do not isolate a single algorithmic cause for resource differences.
Host RSS uses ps and is distinct from MLX active/cache/peak-active allocator accounting; do not subtract counters to attribute allocations or equate either to a hard physical-memory bound.
Old RSS samples are stamped after ps returns; new iteration timestamps precede ps, disk sampling and manifest reading. Exact cross-run or per-frame clock alignment is unavailable.

New progress changes report atomic manifest publication observed after the same iteration RSS sample. Previously observed and later same-iteration counts provide context, not an exact GPU-completion timestamp.
Per-frame MLX snapshots follow four view readbacks/writes and have no host timestamp; no post-teardown MLX snapshot exists.
All samples, missing RSS values and coalesced progress groups are retained. Sampling cannot rule out sub-interval peaks or longer-term retention growth.
Time and progress windows are descriptive; recorded watchdog RSS/MLX/disk/time limits are operational abort policies, not resource or performance acceptance thresholds.
Free-disk measurements are whole-filesystem observations, not exclusive byte accounting for this capture.
Historical revisions/hashes remain unchanged; current source-object checks and pin verification are separate from reported execution measurements.
resources.interpretation: RSS and MLX counters use different accounting. Progress timestamps mark the start of polling iterations, before RSS and later manifest reads; they are not exact frame completion times. Observed peaks and late windows establish neither a hard memory ceiling nor source-rate playback.
